headline: High-risk filesystem and workflow overlap: ECC can write shared state while Rasa can ingest external messages, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write local files, use MCP, and run browsers; Rasa ingests messages from Slack/Messenger/Telegram-style channels. If ECC outputs are bridged into Rasa via shared files or copied prompts, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default integrations, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are copied into a Rasa training or runtime channel without sanitization
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge passes ECC-generated text into Rasa prompts
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of ECC-generated files into Rasa flows
Add a prompt/content sanitizer at the handoff point
Require human review before importing ECC outputs into Rasa
Use separate directories and credentials for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, and can write files; Rasa handles text/voice and connects to external messaging APIs. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose ECC-managed sensitive material to Rasa outputs or third-party channels. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing ECC session files or security findings
IF Rasa is configured to forward conversation content to external messaging APIs
mitigations: Store ECC state outside any Rasa-accessible directory
Redact secrets from ECC exports before handoff
Restrict Rasa channels to non-sensitive test data
Rotate any credentials present in shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has filesystem write, git mutation, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress; Rasa has allowlisted egress and can run as a multi-channel bot. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, they can overwrite each other's files or race on shared mutable resources. No locking is documented, so conflict risk is credible.
conditions: IF ECC and Rasa write to the same repository or config directory
IF both are deployed under the same mutable OAuth or API credentials
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Use git branches instead of direct writes
Snapshot configs before running either agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate code, docs, and security findings; Rasa can turn text inputs into downstream bot responses on messaging channels. If Rasa treats ECC output as authoritative without verification, a mistaken or malicious ECC result can cascade into user-facing actions or advice. The pathway is inferred from both profiles and is not guarded by default.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes ECC-produced text as a source of truth
IF downstream bot responses are sent to end users without human review
mitigations: Require verification before Rasa uses ECC outputs
Limit ECC outputs to drafts, not final responses
Add confidence thresholds and fallback responses
Log and review cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: implement structured schemas for ECC-to-Rasa outputs

E_compliance.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, and session data, while Rasa handles text and voice through messaging platforms. The profiles do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible if regulated data is routed through Rasa channels. ECC is the more relevant citation because its touched data classes are broader; Rasa is cited for channel exposure.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed from ECC into Rasa messaging channels
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Rasa channels
Set short retention on both systems
Document data-class handling for each agent
Review channel logs for sensitive content
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
